slides.title: Sub-Millisecond Reflexes for Continuous Physical Human-Robot Interaction
slides.highlight: This work introduces a sub-millisecond reflex engine for ROS 2 that enables deterministic control switching and safety mitigations, directly supporting the low-latency responsiveness required for safe embodied social robots and human-robot interaction.

card.one_liner: Open-source ROS 2 framework enables sub-millisecond controller switching for uninterrupted, safe human-robot interaction.
card.key_idea: Enhanced multimode controller uses lock-free pointer swaps and pre-allocated resources to eliminate runtime middleware overhead during control transitions.
card.evaluation: Validated on Franka Panda; achieved <0.1ms switching latency, 3.5% faster task completion, and 3x lower jerk versus standard ros2_control baselines.
card.limitation: Reflex behaviors and safety thresholds are predefined and application-dependent, requiring careful manual tuning for specific tasks.

slides.title: CarryOn: A Dual-Loop Harness for Personalized and Reliable Robot Assistance
slides.tldr: ENHANCING VLA ROBOTS WITH PERSONALIZATION AND SAFETY
slides.highlight: CarryOn introduces a dual-loop framework that augments frozen vision-language-action models with persistent user context for personalization and active safety supervision, significantly reducing hazard violations and improving recovery success in real-world robot assistance.

card.one_liner: CarryOn augments frozen VLAs with a dual-loop harness for personalized planning and reliable, safe execution.
card.key_idea: Planning loop grounds tasks in revisable user/scene memory; execution loop combines proactive geometric shielding with reflective recovery skills.
card.evaluation: Tested on real robots and LIBERO/RoboLab simulations, reducing safety violations to 6.1% and boosting recovery success to 80%.
card.limitation: Relies on accurate visual grounding for memory updates and geometric shielding, which may fail in highly cluttered or dynamic scenes.

slides.title: Spark-0: Scaling Spatially Aligned Tactile Pretraining for Robot Dexterous Manipulation
slides.highlight: This work demonstrates how spatially aligned tactile pretraining significantly improves dexterous manipulation success rates, offering insights into integrating touch sensing for embodied learning and human-robot interaction.

card.one_liner: Spark-0 uses tactile supervision for pretraining and tactile input for inference to boost dexterous robot manipulation.
card.key_idea: Spatially aligned VTLA model using tactile contact maps as pretraining supervision and regional force histories as inference conditioning.
card.evaluation: Tested on SparkArena and Ego Humanoid Benchmark; outperforms vision-only baselines with significant success rate gains.
card.limitation: Requires specialized tactile glove data for pretraining and specific hardware for tactile-conditioned real-robot deployment.

slides.title: MAIA: Anticipating Interaction Anomalies in Contact-Rich Manipulation via Multimodal World Models
slides.highlight: This work demonstrates how multimodal world models can proactively anticipate physical interaction anomalies, offering a methodological parallel for HyECHO's goal of predicting emergent states in hybrid human-AI teams before they fully manifest.

card.one_liner: MAIA anticipates contact-rich manipulation anomalies by modeling future visual and force responses of planned actions.
card.key_idea: A vision-action-force world model predicts future multimodal states under planned actions, feeding a lightweight anomaly head for early warning.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on new CRIA dataset (2,852 trajectories); outperforms baselines in bACC and lead time, improving real-robot success from 52.6% to 61.5%.
card.limitation: Limited to 50-step prediction horizon, single robot platform, and lacks root-cause diagnosis or autonomous recovery capabilities.

slides.title: Ego2Contact: Predicting Touch from Egocentric Human Video for Contact-Rich Robot Manipulation
slides.tldr: TRANSFER HUMAN TACTILE PRIORS TO ROBOTS
slides.highlight: This work demonstrates transferring tactile priors learned from human egocentric video to robot hands, addressing the scarcity of robot tactile data. It is relevant to MOSAIC as it provides a method to infer interaction forces and contact locations from visual streams, supporting the estimation of procedural skill and physics-based proficiency in human-AI coadaptation loops.

card.one_liner: Ego2Contact transfers human visual-tactile priors to robots via anatomical mapping to enable contact-rich manipulation.
card.key_idea: Fuses temporal scene context and hand-local features in a flow-matching generator, aligning human tactile grids to robot sensors via anatomical correspondences.
card.evaluation: Validated on EgoTouch/EgoTactile datasets and Isaac Gym simulations; outperforms baselines in tactile prediction and improves policy success rates.
card.limitation: Requires hand-designed anatomical mappings for each robot; predicted touch recovers only partial benefits of ground-truth sensing in complex tasks.

slides.title: Dexterity from Supervised Play
slides.highlight: This work introduces a framework where robots learn dexterous manipulation by autonomously collecting contact-rich data through supervised play, significantly reducing the need for task-specific demonstrations or sim-to-real transfer.

card.one_liner: Robots learn dexterity by autonomously collecting data from human-played policies and planning with a world model.
card.key_idea: Behavior cloning on human play creates a goal-agnostic policy that collects data to train a world model, enabling MPC for task-specific goals.
card.evaluation: Tested on Push-T and in-hand reorientation in simulation and real hardware, outperforming hindsight BC and matching PPO with 490x less data.
card.limitation: Requires initial human teleoperation data; MPC inference is computationally expensive, though mitigated by optional policy distillation.

slides.title: Blind Precise Assembly: Proprioceptive Sim-to-Real Peg-in-Hole for Diverse Parts
slides.highlight: Demonstrates that precise, contact-rich assembly tasks like peg insertion can be achieved using only proprioceptive joint sensing, eliminating the need for visual or tactile inputs. This supports MOSAIC's focus on physics-based skill estimation and procedural skill acquisition by showing how agents can learn robust manipulation strategies through contact dynamics alone.

card.one_liner: Blind sim-to-real policies use only joint proprioception to achieve 73% success in precise peg insertion.
card.key_idea: Reinforcement learning policies trained in simulation observe only joint history, using contact supervision and a procedural generator for exact collision geometry.
card.evaluation: Tested on peg, gear, and nut tasks; zero-shot real-world transfer achieved 73% success, outperforming visual policies on unseen shapes.
card.limitation: Requires initial contact with the fixture and cannot handle global localization or large-scale search errors.

slides.title: No Eyes, No Problem: What Does Touch Contribute to Blind Baoding Ball Manipulation?
slides.highlight: This work demonstrates sustained blind manipulation of Baoding balls on a physical dexterous hand using only proprioception and binary tactile feedback, achieving zero-shot sim-to-real transfer through novel domain randomizations.

card.one_liner: Zero-shot sim-to-real transfer enables blind Baoding ball rotation on hardware using only touch and proprioception.
card.key_idea: Hardware-aligned simulation with tendon coupling, tactile calibration, and novel randomizations (SlewDR, STAT) bridge the sim-to-real gap.
card.evaluation: Tested on Shadow Hand Lite; achieved 34.75 mean rotations and 0.36 rot/s, outperforming baselines in sustained blind manipulation.
card.limitation: High performance variance (std 26.06 rotations) and reliance on specific binary tactile calibration may limit generalization to other objects.
